title: The AI pricing paradox: AI PCs might be the answer to spiralling cloud costs for some, but that doesn't mean cloud…
excerpt: AI PCs will bring pricing predictability, but cloud computing remains essential
content_html:
Now that AI vendors have us hooked and using generative and agentic tools, pricing models are shifting. Subscriptions are no longer loss-making models designed to attract experimental customers, because they now need to serve a much more important purpose – make back money.

How this might look is still largely being figured out, but already we're seeing major software vendors ditch per-seat pricing in favor of token consumption or outcomes.

What this is likely to mean for corporate and enterprise customers is that AI is about to become a whole lot more expensive – but it's not all bad news because these companies also have the opportunity to gain more control over certain spends.

Step forward the AI PC, which is increasingly capable of running small models locally and handling basic and even some mid-level generative tasks without ever needing to spend a cent in the cloud. A few months ago, my social media was even filled with consumers and knowledge workers grabbing Mac minis to run Openclaw's AI agent locally.

A brief overview of how the consumption-based model could look

Shashi Upadhyay, Zendesk's President for Products, Engineering and AI, explained the reason behind the shift we're seeing in pricing models – traditional metrics are becoming less relevant and new metrics are emerging. "We believe software value should align directly with customer success, not headcount," he told me in an interview.

Upadhyay also criticized per-seat models for charging customers for raw AI, whether their problem gets solved or not. But a shift to outcome-based pricing relies on the vendor and customer agreeing "on the exact result that triggers payment."

On the surface, it looks like this could be a variable that might differ on a vendor-by-vendor basis, but thinking about it more deeply, customers would ultimately be able to determine their own meaningful outcome, meaning that they only ever pay for success and never pay for failures.

Gartner Research Director Ranjit Atwal even implied that AI PCs could follow a similar trajectory: "The real question isn’t about definitions—it’s about how PCs deliver AI outcomes." Analyst projections have AI PCs (equipped with NPUs) accounting for 95% of the market by 2029.

Distinguishing the needs of local processing vs. cloud compute

With this emerging hybrid split of use cases in mind, it would mean enterprises can pay a one-time set price for an AI PC and workers will have unlimited access to on-device processing for tasks like summarization, transcription, image background removal and more.

It leaves cloud – the more unpredictable expense – only for the tasks that require extra compute, such as huge enterprise applications that handle centralized data, or running the latest and most powerful models.

I set out to determine what exactly makes an AI PC and how analysts expect this shift to impact the relevant markets, but Omdia’s research director for PC and tablet research Ishan Dutt warned me that we're still living through this transition, so quite how the end looks is yet to be determined.

For example, Dutt explained that so-called 'AI-ready' PCs just 18 months ago would've had sub-10 TOPS NPUs. But then came along Microsoft's own classification of Copilot+ PCs with around 40 TOPS. Just recently at CES 2025, Intel, AMD and Qualcomm all showed 50+ TOPS NPUs, and we're already seeing hints of 75+ TOPS.

Market intelligence firms like Omdia would typically classify an AI PC as one possessing a Neural Processing Unit (NPU), "designed for running AI workloads locally alongside the CPU/GPU," Dutt told me, but this is clearly a new category whose ceiling is still being pushed by chipmakers, and whose baseline is still being written.

Other, more traditional metrics are also relevant in the world of local processing, with Omdia implying that 16GB or memory is barely sufficient these days. Anything more than lightweight tasks is more likely to benefit from 32GB+.

"In practice, 'AI-capability' is really a function of three hardware considerations (NPU TOPS, RAM, and increasingly GPU for generative/creative workloads), not a single number," Dutt told me in an exclusive interview. "I’d expect the bar to keep moving as agentic, always-on background AI workloads become the reference use case rather than chat-style assistants."

AI PC demand vs. the effects of the device refresh cycle

Having determined the parameters that broadly define an AI PC, I wanted to understand whether enterprises are actually kitting staff out with them today. I've read many a study about the increasing unpredictability of cloud-based AI pricing, and data even shows that AI PC shipments are rising. But is this indicative of a shift away from cloud-exclusive processing, or is it just that more PCs now classify as AI PCs anyway, and generic refresh cycles are impacting these numbers with false positives?

"NPUs are now the baseline across new Intel, AMD and Qualcomm platforms," Dutt said, before reminding that me that Macs have had NPUs since the 2020 move to Apple silicon, which came around two years before ChatGPT went public.

Omdia's market analysis projects that the AI PC (equipped with an NPU) market share among all PCs will reach 77.5% by 2030, compared with 17.3% in 2024. Analysts also note that the Windows 10 end of life concentrated a large number of upgrades over the past year or two, bringing AI PC market share up considerably.

Gartner's Atwal is more optimistic that organizations will focus more on PCs that "play a strategic role in AI workflows and business outcomes," indicating there will be at least some thought into buying higher-end devices.

Dutt explained that "clearer outlining of how hardware upgrades unlock future on-device AI functionality" could further impact the cadence of refresh cycles, while Atwal sees the greatest success coming from OEMs who can help "alleviate the token crisis" by connecting cloud to edge.

AI PCs have a pricing problem of their own

"Consumption-based cloud AI pricing does create a genuine total cost of ownership argument for shifting inference workloads on-device," Dutt agreed, however the PC market has its own challenges that are also leasing to pricing instability.

While it may seem like we've been living through a chip shortage for half a decade, we've actually been in two – and this second one is probably much worse.

The earlier 2020-2022 shortage was a "pandemic-driven demand/logistics mismatch," which normalized pretty quickly. This second shortage is a "deliberate capacity reallocation as memory makers are shifting DRAM/NAND wafer capacity toward HBM and high-capacity DDR5," Dutt told me. In other words, the problem we're looking to solve (AI-driving pricing instability) is being driven by itself (enterprise AI consumption). A Catch-22, if you like.

With Apple recently doing the unthinkable and raising prices across most Mac models, or cutting entry-level models altogether, Omdia sets out the challenges that lay ahead: 60% of channel partners expect to experience either delays (53%) or outright cancellations (7%) of their customers’ hardware refresh plans.

Already, 70% of channel partners are expecting major shortages across some (11%) or most (59%) of their PC hardware products.

Through 2026-2027, Gartner is preparing for reduced sales, but 2028 could mark an inflection point where memory prices drop and agentic AI matures, pushing forward a new replacement cycle.

The future is hybrid

Returning to my original theory that many organizational AI workloads will shift to local processing amid an evolving cloud subscription landscape, it's increasingly clear that a rise in AI PC shipments doesn't necessarily correlate with genuine customer demand.

While shifting some processing to run locally has huge merits when looking at the cloud compute market in isolation, the PC market's own challenges complicate strategies further. The answer will likely involve a hybrid approach to both sides, but how that hybrid and split will look will vary case-by-case.

But more crucially, cloud processing isn't set to go anywhere, and it will continue to complement local workloads with the type of power and performance that few organizations could ever afford to acquire. Upadhyay reminded me that cloud compute's benefits span "centralizing multi-channel customer data, real-time ticket routing, unified reporting, and seamless API integrations across hundreds of tools."

blocks.html_en: Having determined the parameters that broadly define an AI PC, I wanted to understand whether enterprises are actually kitting staff out with them today. I've read many a study about the increasing unpredictability of cloud-based AI pricing, and data even shows that AI PC shipments are rising. But is this indicative of a shift away from cloud-exclusive processing, or is it just that more PCs now classify as AI PCs anyway, and generic refresh cycles are impacting these numbers with false positives?

blocks.html_en: While it may seem like we've been living through a chip shortage for half a decade, we've actually been in two – and this second one is probably much worse.

sentences.zh: 虽然我们似乎已经经历了五年的芯片短缺，但实际上已经经历了两次——而第二次可能更糟。

blocks.html_en: The earlier 2020-2022 shortage was a "pandemic-driven demand/logistics mismatch," which normalized pretty quickly. This second shortage is a "deliberate capacity reallocation as memory makers are shifting DRAM/NAND wafer capacity toward HBM and high-capacity DDR5," Dutt told me. In other words, the problem we're looking to solve (AI-driving pricing instability) is being driven by itself (enterprise AI consumption). A Catch-22, if you like.

content_html_zh:
现在人工智能供应商让我们着迷并使用生成和代理工具，定价模型正在发生变化。 订阅不再是旨在吸引实验客户的亏损模式，因为它们现在需要服务于一个更重要的目的——赚钱。

这可能看起来如何，很大程度上仍在弄清楚，但我们已经看到主要软件供应商放弃按席位定价，转而支持代币消费或结果。

对于企业和企业客户来说，这可能意味着人工智能将变得更加昂贵——但这并不全是坏消息，因为这些公司还有机会获得对某些支出的更多控制权。

AI PC 更进一步，它越来越有能力在本地运行小型模型并处理基本甚至一些中级生成任务，而无需在云端花费一分钱。 几个月前，我的社交媒体上甚至充斥着消费者和知识工作者拿起 Mac mini 在本地运行 Openclaw 的 AI 代理。

基于消费的模型的简要概述

Zendesk 产品、工程和人工智能总裁 Shashi Upadhyay 解释了我们在定价模型中看到的转变背后的原因 - 传统指标的相关性越来越低，新指标不断出现。 “我们相信软件价值应该与客户的成功直接挂钩，而不是与员工数量挂钩，”他在接受采访时告诉我。

Upadhyay 还批评按座位模式向客户收取原始人工智能费用，无论他们的问题是否得到解决。 但转向基于结果的定价取决于供应商和客户就“触发付款的确切结果”达成一致。

从表面上看，这可能是一个因供应商而异的变量，但更深入地思考，客户最终将能够确定自己有意义的结果，这意味着他们只为成功付费，而从不为失败付费。

订阅 TechRadar Pro 时事通讯，获取您的企业成功所需的所有热门新闻、观点、功能和指导！

Gartner 研究总监 Ranjit Atwal 甚至暗示 AI PC 可能会遵循类似的轨迹：“真正的问题不在于定义，而在于 PC 如何提供 AI 结果。” 分析师预测，到 2029 年，人工智能 PC（配备 NPU）将占据 95% 的市场份额。

区分本地处理与云计算的需求

考虑到这种新兴的混合用例，这意味着企业可以一次性支付一台人工智能电脑的固定价格，而工作人员将可以无限制地访问设备上的处理任务，例如摘要、转录、图像背景去除等。

它让云——更不可预测的费用——只用于需要额外计算的任务，例如处理集中数据的大型企业应用程序，或运行最新、最强大的模型。

我着手确定人工智能 PC 的真正含义以及分析师预计这种转变将如何影响相关市场，但 Omdia 的 PC 和平板电脑研究总监 Ishan Dutt 警告我，我们仍在经历这一转变，因此最终的结果尚未确定。

例如，Dutt 解释说，就在 18 个月前，所谓的“AI 就绪”PC 还拥有低于 10 TOPS 的 NPU。 但随后出现了微软自己的 Copilot+ PC 分类，大约有 40 TOPS。 就在最近的 CES 2025 上，英特尔、AMD 和高通都展示了 50+ TOPS NPU，而且我们已经看到了 75+ TOPS 的迹象。

像 Omdia 这样的市场情报公司通常会将 AI PC 归类为拥有神经处理单元 (NPU) 的 PC，“专为与 CPU/GPU 一起在本地运行 AI 工作负载而设计”，Dutt 告诉我，但这显然是一个新类别，芯片制造商仍在推动其上限，其基准仍在制定中。

其他更传统的指标也与本地处理领域相关，Omdia 暗示目前 16GB 或内存几乎不够。 任何轻量级任务都更有可能从 32GB+ 中受益。

“实际上，‘人工智能能力’实际上是三个硬件考虑因素的函数（NPU TOPS、RAM 以及越来越多的用于生成/创意工作负载的 GPU），而不是一个数字，”杜特在一次独家采访中告诉我。 “我预计这个标准会继续发展，因为代理、始终在线的后台人工智能工作负载将成为参考用例，而不是聊天式的助手。”

AI PC 需求与设备刷新周期的影响

在确定了人工智能电脑的大致定义参数后，我想了解企业现在是否真的在为员工配备人工智能电脑。 我读过很多关于基于云的人工智能定价越来越不可预测的研究，数据甚至显示人工智能 PC 的出货量正在上升。 但这是否表明云专有处理的转变，或者只是越来越多的电脑现在被归类为人工智能电脑，而通用刷新周期正在通过误报影响这些数字？

“NPU 现在是新的英特尔、AMD 和高通平台的基准，”Dutt 说道，然后提醒我，自 2020 年转向苹果芯片以来，Mac 就已经配备了 NPU，而苹果芯片是在 ChatGPT 上市前两年左右出现的。

Omdia的市场分析预计，到2030年，AI PC（配备NPU）在所有PC中的市场份额将达到77.5%，而2024年为17.3%。 分析师还指出，Windows 10 的生命周期结束集中在过去一两年内进行了大量升级，使 AI PC 市场份额大幅上升。

Gartner 的阿特瓦尔更为乐观地认为，组织将更多地关注“在人工智能工作流程和业务成果中发挥战略作用”的个人电脑，这表明至少会有一些考虑购买更高端的设备。

Dutt 解释说，“更清晰地概述硬件升级如何解锁未来设备上的人工智能功能”可能会进一步影响刷新周期的节奏，而 Atwal 认为最大的成功来自 OEM，他们可以通过将云连接到边缘来帮助“缓解令牌危机”。

人工智能电脑也有自己的定价问题

Dutt 表示同意：“基于消费的云 AI 定价确实为将推理工作负载转移到设备上创造了真正的总拥有成本论据。”然而，PC 市场也面临着自身的挑战，这些挑战也导致了定价不稳定。

虽然我们似乎已经经历了五年的芯片短缺，但实际上已经经历了两次——而第二次可能更糟。

2020-2022 年早些时候的短缺是“疫情驱动的需求/物流不匹配”，但很快就正常化了。 Dutt 告诉我，第二个短缺是“故意的产能重新分配，因为内存制造商正在将 DRAM/NAND 晶圆产能转向 HBM 和高容量 DDR5”。 换句话说，我们想要解决的问题（人工智能驱动的定价不稳定）是由其本身（企业人工智能消费）驱动的。 如果你愿意的话，可以说是第二十二条军规。

随着 Apple 最近对大多数 Mac 机型采取了难以想象的提价措施，或者完全削减入门级机型，Omdia 列出了未来面临的挑战：60% 的渠道合作伙伴预计客户的硬件更新计划要么会延迟 (53%)，要么会彻底取消 (7%)。

70% 的渠道合作伙伴预计其部分 (11%) 或大部分 (59%) PC 硬件产品将出现严重短缺。

Gartner 正在为 2026 年至 2027 年销量减少做好准备，但 2028 年可能标志着内存价格下降和代理 AI 成熟的拐点，从而推动新的更换周期。

未来是混合动力

回到我最初的理论，即在不断发展的云订阅环境中，许多组织的人工智能工作负载将转向本地处理，越来越明显的是，人工智能 PC 出货量的增长并不一定与真正的客户需求相关。

虽然在孤立地看待云计算市场时，将一些处理转移到本地运行具有巨大的优点，但 PC 市场本身的挑战使策略进一步复杂化。 答案可能涉及双方采取混合方法，但混合和拆分的方式将根据具体情况而有所不同。

但更重要的是，云处理不会走向任何地方，它将继续以很少有组织能够负担得起的能力和性能来补充本地工作负载。 Upadhyay 提醒我，云计算的好处涵盖“集中多渠道客户数据、实时票务路由、统一报告以及跨数百种工具的无缝 API 集成”。
